title: How Morgellons Disease Works
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck examine Morgellons disease, a mysterious condition first described in 2002 by Mary Leitao, whose toddler son had sores with strange fibers around his lips. Sufferers report fibers emerging from skin, itching, stinging and a sensation of bugs burrowing under the skin. Oklahoma State pharmacology professor Randy Wymore tested fibers that could not be matched in the FBI database; lab results later identified cotton, nylon, human and rodent hair, goose down and a possible fungal fiber. A 2008 CDC study, prompted by letters to Congress, concluded there was no infectious or environmental cause, that sores came from chronic scratching, and that many participants had psychiatric or drug-use issues; the medical establishment largely treats it as delusional parasitosis. The episode covers the "matchbox sign," the difficulty sufferers face being taken seriously, itch researcher Louise Oaklander's view that it is a chronic itch disorder, and UK doctor Nick Mann's account of finding tropical rat mites. The episode also includes a listener mail about the MPAA X rating history and sponsor reads.

segments.title: Introduction to Morgellons
segments.summary: Hosts introduce Morgellons, the name borrowed from a 17th-century French medical text, and the 2002 case of Mary Leitao's toddler son with fibers in sores around his lips.

segments.title: Mysterious fibers and Randy Wymore's testing
segments.summary: Description of colored fibers from skin sores and Oklahoma State pharmacology professor Randy Wymore's attempts to identify them, which failed to match the FBI fiber database.

segments.title: Symptoms and sufferer experiences
segments.summary: Sufferers report bug-like burrowing sensations, gritty feelings under eyelids, intense itching, and compulsive picking; anecdotes include a man removing a fiber from his eyeball with tweezers.

segments.title: CDC 2008 study and medical dismissal
segments.summary: After thousands wrote to Congress, the CDC studied Morgellons in 2008 and found no infectious or environmental cause, attributed sores to scratching, and noted psychiatric and drug-use findings among participants.

segments.title: Chicken-or-egg problem and the matchbox sign
segments.summary: Discussion of whether psychological distress results from being dismissed or causes the symptoms, the matchbox sign in which doctors dismiss patients who bring in samples, and the catch-22 this creates.

segments.title: Itch research and Randy Wymore's lab results
segments.summary: Harvard itch specialist Louise Oaklander's view that Morgellons may be a chronic itch disorder, the 1987 German finding that itch has its own nerve network, and lab results identifying cotton, nylon, hair, down and possible fungal fibers.

segments.title: Nick Mann's case and tropical rat mites
segments.summary: UK general practitioner Nick Mann describes his self-treatment and a mite identified as a tropical rat mite; hosts note the lack of research and labs' reluctance to test fibers.

segments.title: Ongoing debate and need for help
segments.summary: Hosts discuss theories ranging from mites to nanotechnology and conspiracy claims, and argue that sufferers need help regardless of cause.

segments.title: Listener mail: MPAA X rating history
segments.summary: Listener Dan from UCLA adds history of the X rating, including Jack Valenti, Midnight Cowboy, self-rated X films, and Wes Craven's The Last House on the Left.

segments.title: Outro and contact information
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and invite feedback by Twitter, Facebook, email and the website.
